rationale: The student includes the starting number in their count instead of counting hops/movements. Modeling subtraction on a number line with clear individual backwards hops reinforces that the count begins after the first jump, landing on the next number.

script.focus: Notice that the first hop moves from 14 to 13, so counting begins on 13.

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: Notice that the first hop moves from 14 to 13, so counting begins on 13.

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration explicitly addresses the exact misconception ('Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet. Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.'). It breaks down the movement step-by-step and uses a clean worked example (14 - 4) without spoiling the student's problem (12 - 3).
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this clear worked demonstration because it directly addresses the student's off-by-one counting error.
